task: Speed up FermiNet training steps for Fe, Kr, Cd, Xe with results bit-for-bit identical to the original
constraints: one generic optimization set for all four atoms; no per-element or per-electron-count code paths
bit-wise identical to the original (deterministic XLA mode), every recorded step
upstream hyper-parameters, precision and random streams unchanged

workload.precision: upstream (float32 params; XLA default dot precision)

bench_only.note: one-off phases shortened; the timed training step is unchanged

hardware.parallelism: four independent single-GPU runs (Fe, Kr, Cd, Xe), one per GPU

gates.timing: default XLA flags; ABA in independent processes; median of 3x5-step windows after compile + 2 warm-up steps; pass if speedup > max(1.02, 1 + 2*|A-B|/mean) and window range < 10%
gates.bitwise: XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true for both trees; per step energy bits, pmove, sha256 of all leaves of walkers/params/opt_state/mcmc_width; 8 steps (+110 steps for the final candidate)
gates.kernel_probe: bench/trsm_check.py: Pallas solve vs real cuBLAS, n in 9..64, 4 variants, 3 input scales, 0 mismatches
gates.reference_self_check: reference reproduces itself bit for bit in deterministic mode (done twice before any candidate)

note: evaluator_sha256 covers the published bench files; their measurement logic is the one used for the recorded runs (only machine-identifying fingerprint fields were removed for publication).
